gary_2026_10_07_pmai_creativity_business.title: PMAI - Creativity & Business Problems In Age Of AI
gary_2026_10_07_pmai_creativity_business.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_10_07_pmai_creativity_business.summary: Gary's Guide: Creativity & Business Problems in the Age of AI - a workshop for entrepreneurs We are entering a strange moment for creativity. For decades, we have been taught that innovation comes from thinking outside the box, brainstorming more ideas, & waiting for that breakthrough moment. But in the age of AI, & ideas are suddenly abundant, the real challenge is no longer simply coming up with more ideas. It is knowing how to find the right pieces, make unexpected connections, & turn them into something genuinely new & useful. This hands-on workshop, led by our head of program Jeffrey, introduces a practical methodology for doing exactly that. What we'll cover We'll start by looking at some of the traditional assumptions behind creativity & innovation: brainstorming, originality, intuition, & the idea of the lone creative genius, & why some of those assumptions are becoming less useful in an AI-native world. We'll then introduce a different way to approach creative problem-solving: instead of trying to invent the answer from scratch, you'll learn how to break a problem apart, deliberately search for useful precedents & ideas, & recombine existing elements in new ways. Through real-world case studies, we'll examine how successful products, businesses, & innovations often emerge not from a completely original idea, but from making the right connection between things that already exist. Most importantly, this will not be a lecture. You'll work through the methodology yourself, apply it to actual business problems, & leave with a framework you can reuse when thinking about products, positioning, growth, operations, or your next startup idea. Who should attend This workshop is designed primarily for: Early-stage founders, aspiring entrepreneurs, small business owners, product builders, & operators who regularly need to solve ambiguous problems with limited resources. No technical background is required. If you have ever stared at a blank page thinking, I need a better idea, this workshop is for you. Come with a problem. Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

gary_2026_10_07_sovereign_ai_at_applicat.summary: Gary's Guide: An AI Alliance Meetup, co-hosted with Neo4j & IBM | October 7, 2026 | IBM One Madison Avenue, New York Every enterprise now has the same problem in a different form. The data that would make a model useful is the data you are not allowed to move. It sits inside one firm, under one regulator, in a schema few have mapped. The interesting work in AI has quietly shifted from training bigger models alone to developing systems to utilize the data enterprises have. This afternoon is about how that is actually built. Potential topic areas: Context. Structuring the data inside a firm so a model may reason. Federation. Connecting institutions to train & evaluate to move an industry forward. Privacy. The architecture that makes cross-institution work permissible. Regulation. Why banks are now being asked to do this. What institutions may or may not allow connecting with closed models. Aligned with these topics sits Project Tapestry, the AI Alliance's consortium driven open-weights model effort. We will open with where it stands: Milestone 0 complete, Milestone 1 underway, & the ecosystem as it develops. This is a technical afternoon for engineers, architects, & data leads. Join with hard questions & connect with others facing similar challenges. In this fast-paced, emergency-response-themed hackathon, participants will compete in teams of 2-4 across a series of short challenges designed to test how quickly you can understand a problem, make decisions, build a solution, & communicate your thinking under pressure. Each round will introduce a new emergency-response scenario. Your team will have roughly 45 minutes to develop & submit a solution before moving immediately into the next challenge. No long build cycle. No endless polishing. You'll have to prioritize what matters, divide responsibilities quickly, & make tradeoffs in real time. How It Works Participants will form teams of 2-4 people. Over the course of the event, teams will face 3-4 short emergency-response challenges, revealed one at a time. For each round: A new problem is announced Teams have approximately 45 minutes to respond Teams submit their solution before the deadline Judges score the submissions The next challenge begins Scores accumulate across the rounds, & the team with the strongest overall performance wins. The challenges may involve areas such as emergency coordination, communication, resource allocation, information management, public safety, or rapid decision-making. What Are We Looking For? You do not need to build a fully finished product. Depending on the challenge, your submission could be a prototype, workflow, AI agent, product concept, operational system, or another practical solution. What matters is your ability to: Identify the real problem. Prioritize under pressure. Build quickly. Make smart tradeoffs. Explain why your solution works. Who Should Join? Come with teammates or meet people at the event. Why Rapid Fire? Real emergencies rarely give you perfect information, unlimited resources, or weeks to plan. jc_culture_43584_2026_11_05_flame_the_ex.summary: Flame (The Experience) for a one night only event presented by Ruby Hawk Productions and Art House Productions in Jersey City, New Jersey.
